user.title: Connect to Crestron processor
user.description: Home Assistant will open a TCP server on this port. Configure your Crestron program to connect to Home Assistant's IP address on this port using the XSIG symbol.

error.invalid_join: Invalid join: use d123 (digital), a123 (analog) or s123 (serial).
error.join_out_of_range: Join out of range: digital joins go from 1 to 4096, analog and serial joins from 1 to 1024.
error.invalid_divisor: Invalid divisor: it must be greater than 0 (10 = one decimal, 1 = no decimals).
error.invalid_temp_unit: Choose Home Assistant unit, Celsius, or Fahrenheit for processor temperatures.
error.invalid_mute_mode: Choose a supported mute join behavior.
error.invalid_position_scale: Choose a supported position value range.
error.invalid_number_range: Invalid range: maximum value must be greater than minimum value and the step must be greater than 0.
error.brightness_out_of_range: Default brightness must be an integer between 0 and 255.
error.rgb_joins_incomplete: Configure all three RGB joins (red, green and blue), or leave all three empty.
error.duplicate_light_joins: Brightness and RGB joins must use distinct analog join numbers.
error.value_out_of_range: Value out of range: the analog range is 0-65535.
error.invalid_presets: Invalid presets: use 'Name:join' pairs with digital joins 1-4096 (e.g. Home:21).
error.missing_join: A join is required (e.g. a101, d451, s7).
error.missing_source: Provide a value_template or an entity_id (at least one).

overview.title: Crestron XSIG overview
overview.description:
Inventory of configured entities, joins, exposes and actions. Script contents are not displayed. Download a JSON export from the integration's Download diagnostics menu. Review the file before sharing it, as it contains configured templates and scripts.

{summary}

add_switch.title: Add switch
add_switch.description: For all field details, examples and wiring screenshots, see the [Switch help guide]({help_url}). Join direction: (XSIG in -> HA) = data sent by the processor, (XSIG out <- HA) = data sent to the processor, (XSIG in+out) = both.

data.name: Name
data.switch_join: Digital join (XSIG in+out: state feedback + command)
data.optimistic: Optimistic: update the state immediately, without waiting for the processor to echo the join back
data.state_sync: State sync: keep the XSIG join updated with the real state of the entity, also when it changes for reasons other than your command (e.g. feedback from Crestron). Use ONLY if your program reads this join as a level (on/off state), not as a pulse/toggle command: a pulse-driven program could oscillate.

add_cover.title: Add cover
add_cover.description: For all field details, examples and wiring screenshots, see the [Cover help guide]({help_url}). Only the name is required. Configure the joins your setup actually has, combining them freely: digital pulses, analog position and feedback. Directions: (XSIG in -> HA) = sent by the processor, (XSIG out <- HA) = sent to the processor, (XSIG in+out) = both sides. Open and close use their digital pulses when configured; enable position commands to also send the position value. Without a pulse, the position join commands that direction.

data.open_join: Digital join - open pulse (XSIG out <- HA, optional)
data.close_join: Digital join - close pulse (XSIG out <- HA, optional)
data.stop_join: Digital join - stop pulse (XSIG out <- HA, optional)
data.is_opening_join: Digital join - is opening (XSIG in -> HA, optional)
data.is_closing_join: Digital join - is closing (XSIG in -> HA, optional)
data.is_closed_join: Digital join - is closed (XSIG in -> HA, optional)
data.is_opened_join: Digital join - is opened / fully open (XSIG in -> HA, optional)
data.position_commands: Also send the position command (closed/open) together with the open/close pulses
data.optimistic: Optimistic: update the state immediately, without waiting for the processor to echo the join back

add_climate.title: Add climate (thermostat)
add_climate.description: For all field details, examples and wiring screenshots, see the [Climate / thermostat help guide]({help_url}). Only the name and the current temperature are required. One setpoint join = single setpoint, two = heat/cool range. Directions: (XSIG in -> HA) = sent by the processor, (XSIG out <- HA) = sent to the processor, (XSIG in+out) = both. Stage/valve feedback (H1/H2/C1/C2/FA) is read-only: wire the active stages or the valve command there so HA can show the HVAC action.

import_legacy.title: Import legacy crestron.yaml
import_legacy.description: Paste the complete content of the old crestron.yaml here, preserving its line breaks and indentation, then confirm. to_joins become exposes (HA -> Crestron), from_joins become actions (Crestron -> HA). You can open the file in a text editor and copy its contents; direct file upload is not supported.

manage_devices.title: Manage devices
manage_devices.description: Devices group entities in the Home Assistant UI. Assign each entity to one of these devices from its own form; entities with no device stay under the integration (Crestron processor).

add_device.title: Add device
add_device.description: Create a device of this integration. It shows up in the devices list and entities assigned to it are grouped under it.

remove_device.title: Remove devices
remove_device.description: Entities assigned to a removed device go back to the integration device. The device itself is deleted.
